title: Fitting insulating plasterboard to a cold external wall
subtitle: Fix rigid-foam-backed insulated plasterboard to an external wall using adhesive dabs and mechanical fixings to add thermal insulation without a stud frame
excerpt: How to fit insulated plasterboard to a cold external wall using adhesive dabs and mechanical fixings, from setting-out board positions through to taping joints and skim finishing.
sourceNotes: British Gypsum White Book technical guidance (open access). UK trade practice for internal wall insulation and NHBC Standards Chapter 6.9 (referenced, not reproduced).

glossaryTerms.definition: A composite board consisting of a plasterboard face bonded to a rigid-foam insulation layer, most commonly PIR (polyisocyanurate) foam. Available in combined thicknesses of 37.5 to 100 mm. It is fixed to the masonry and provides both the insulation layer and the finish surface for skimming or taping.

A point in the construction where a material with higher thermal conductivity than the surrounding insulation bypasses the insulation layer, allowing heat to travel through the building fabric. At fixings through insulated boards, a screw through the foam creates a small thermal bridge; using a short dab of adhesive with a screw limit reduces this.

A low-permeability membrane placed on the warm side of the insulation to resist the migration of water vapour from the heated interior through the construction. In insulated plasterboard installations, the PIR foam itself acts as the vapour check; all joints and perimeter edges should be taped to maintain continuity.

content.text: Insulated plasterboard is a rigid-foam layer bonded to a plasterboard face, fixed to a cold external wall using adhesive dabs and mechanical fixings. It adds insulation without a stud frame. INTERMEDIATE: setting-out accuracy matters, as the boards are fixed permanently and carry the finish surface.
Prepare the wall and set out the board thickness

The masonry must be dry and free from active damp. Identify and mark any pipes or cables buried in the masonry before they are hidden. Using the spirit level, mark a plumb line at each corner of the room representing the finished face of the
. Remember that the total thickness of the board (foam plus plasterboard) comes into the room: plan electrical socket positions for surface-mounted or extended back boxes before fixing begins.

Apply ribbons of low-expansion foam adhesive or dabs of plasterboard adhesive at 300 mm centres across the wall area. Press each board onto the adhesive, checking it is plumb and in plane with adjacent boards. At each fixing point, drive a 100 to 130 mm screw through the board and foam into the masonry, using a low-emissivity fixing to minimise
. Use a minimum of four fixings per board.
Tape all board joints with foil tape to maintain the continuity of the

formed by the foam layer. Seal the perimeter of the wall at floor, ceiling, and side walls with a bead of flexible sealant or expanding foam. Then apply scrim tape over the plasterboard face joints and fill with jointing compound in two coats, feathering the edges well.

Score the plasterboard face with a utility knife along a straight batten and snap the board. Cut the PIR foam with a fine-toothed saw or a long, sharp knife drawn along a guide. PIR dust is an irritant: wear a dust mask and eye protection. Boards can also be cut with a jigsaw fitted with a fine blade.

attrs.symptom: Condensation appears along the perimeter of the boarded wall after installation
attrs.cause: The perimeter seal between the board and the surrounding construction was not completed, allowing warm moist air to reach the cold masonry behind.
attrs.fix: Apply a continuous bead of flexible sealant around the full perimeter of the board, sealing to floor, ceiling, and the return walls.

attrs.symptom: Board face bows in the centre of a large panel
attrs.cause: Too few adhesive dabs or mechanical fixings for the board size.
attrs.fix: Add extra fixings through the board face into the masonry. Use a long screw and a low-profile anchor appropriate for the masonry type.
